defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches file objects, so path-string, devnull, and IO log outputs are never closed in stop()
os.close(self.log_output) raises OSError on a second stop() call (not idempotent)
votes.evidence_quote: `isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO)` is `False` for every file object. `typing.TextIO` is not runtime-checkable; `isinstance(io.TextIOWrapper(...), TextIO)` returns `False` on Python 3.12+. As a result, no file opened by `open()` is ever closed
votes.justification: The review identifies the faulty isinstance(TextIO) check in stop(). It notes that real file objects, including the devnull BufferedWriter, never match, so files stay open. It suggests io.IOBase or a close check, which matches the known defect.
